question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

The candidate said, "I am campaigning in three constituencies this week."
option_1: The candidate said that he is campaigning in three constituencies this week.
option_2: The candidate said that he was campaigning in three constituencies that week.
option_3: The candidate said that he had been campaigning in three constituencies that week.
option_4: The candidate said that he campaigns in three constituencies that week.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The candidate said that he was campaigning in three constituencies that week.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The present continuous ("am campaigning") backshifts to the past continuous ("was campaigning"), and "this week" shifts to "that week".

◦ Complete sentence: The candidate said that he was campaigning in three constituencies that week.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...is campaigning...this week." — the present continuous is wrongly left unchanged instead of backshifting to the past continuous.

 

• Option 3: "...had been campaigning...that week." — the past perfect continuous is an incorrect over-backshift.

 

• Option 4: "...campaigns...that week." — the simple present drops the continuous aspect, which must be preserved.

 

NOTE

 

• He said, "I am attending three conferences this month." → he said that he was attending three conferences that month (present continuous → past continuous; time-word shift).

question:

option_2: The fire officer said to the residents, "Not use the lift during the fire drill."
option_3: The fire officer said to the residents, "Do not use the lift during the fire drill."

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The fire officer said to the residents, "Do not use the lift during the fire drill.".

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An order reported with "ordered...not to" un-backshifts to the negative imperative: "Do not use the lift".

◦ Complete sentence: The fire officer said to the residents, "Do not use the lift during the fire drill."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Do not using the lift..." — the gerund "using" is wrongly used instead of the base verb "use" after "Do not".

 

• Option 2: "Not use the lift..." — the auxiliary "Do" is missing; a negative imperative requires "Do not use", not "Not use".

 

• Option 4: "...You must not use the lift..." — the modal "must" is an unwarranted addition; the order un-backshifts to a plain negative imperative.

 

NOTE

 

• The guard ordered the visitors not to feed the animals. → the guard said to the visitors, "Do not feed the animals." (ordered...not to → negative imperative, in un-backshifting).

question:

The sergeant shouted to the recruits, "Fall in line and stand at attention immediately!"
option_1: The sergeant ordered the recruits falling in line and standing at attention immediately.

option_3: The sergeant ordered the recruits to fall in line and stand at attention immediately.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The sergeant ordered the recruits to fall in line and stand at attention immediately.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A compound imperative reports both commands as parallel to-infinitives, joined by "and", with the second infinitive marker "to" usually omitted for the second verb.

◦ Complete sentence: The sergeant ordered the recruits to fall in line and stand at attention immediately.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...falling in line and standing at attention..." — both verbs are wrongly converted into gerunds instead of the required to-infinitive forms.

 

• Option 2: "...that fall in line and stand at attention..." — the ungrammatical use of "that" followed by bare verbs is incorrect.

 

• Option 4: "...to fall in line and to standing at attention..." — the verb forms are inconsistent; the second verb wrongly uses the gerund "standing" instead of the parallel form "stand".

 

NOTE

 

• The coach shouted, "Run faster and finish the lap!" → the coach ordered them to run faster and finish the lap (compound imperative → parallel to-infinitives).
